composite_prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: complete original scene composite C for the game 零点杂货铺, S01 exterior, daytime. This is a full scene painting, not a UI mockup.
Input Image 1 is STYLE REFERENCE ONLY. Match its coarse matte gouache brushwork, hand-drawn colored-pencil edges, muted colors and deliberately sparse composition; do not copy its indoor subject.
Scene subject: exterior of a two-storey old stone and timber curio shop on a quiet cobbled lane, a simple round-arched display window, a plain solid wooden entrance door, one wisteria vine directly above the entrance, two simple pots of herbs, and ONE small physically crescent-shaped wooden hanging sign on a simple iron bracket, with no text or plaque. A few broad sage tree leaves form a readable canopy at the upper-left edge; a small soft-edged cloud is visible in the open sky.
Composition: wide 16:9 landscape, edge-to-edge painted artwork. The shop is the single clear focal point in the left two thirds. Rightmost 30 percent is a broad quiet low-detail cream plaster return wall and empty lane; bottom 12 percent is broad simple cobbles with little detail. Keep architectural supports and frame joints plausible, avoid excessive symmetry. No shelves, stock items, street crowds, ornate shopfront or decorative clutter.
STYLE_V2: gouache picture-book illustration, visible brush strokes and dry-brush edges, slightly wobbly hand-drawn colored-pencil outlines, simplified shapes, slightly imperfect perspective, limited palette of seven muted colors (cream, warm grey, walnut brown, sage green, dusty teal, faded plum, ochre), soft diffuse daylight, cool-tinted shadows, generous empty wall and floor space, only a few props, one clear focal point, calm and quiet, matte paper texture, no text, no people.
NEGATIVE: glow, bloom, light rays, god rays, lens flare, bokeh, depth of field blur, gold filigree, ornate carvings, glossy or plastic surfaces, hyper-detailed clutter, photorealism, symmetrical fantasy composition, wisteria everywhere, text, letters, numbers, UI, labels, blank labels, blank plaques, rectangular hanging signs, interface frames, borders.
Requested native size 2560×1440 if available, otherwise the tool's actual largest native 16:9 output. Do not draw resolution text.
cleanplate_prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit.
Asset type: S01 DAY raw cleanplate B_all for actual same-position extraction of game layers.
Input Image 1 is the exact EDIT TARGET. This is a local removal/edit, not a new scene. Remove ALL of these movable pieces from the existing painting and fill their previous locations with the plausible wall, roof, timber or sky behind them:
1. The leafy tree canopy at upper-left; retain the static main bare trunk and thick branches wherever visible, but remove the leaves.
2. The entire wisteria vine immediately above and down the left side of the entrance, including leaves, flowers and its winding vine stem. Restore the simple plaster and timber behind it.
3. The small crescent-shaped hanging wooden sign at upper-right of the door, including its little hanging chain and supporting metal bracket; restore plain cream wall.
4. The small white cloud in the sky.
Keep the entrance door and ring handle, all window panes and frames, stone wall, timber structure, roof, both herb pots, cobbled foreground, overall camera and crop EXACTLY as they are. Preserve all unedited pixels as closely as possible. Add no new objects, openings, labels or decoration. This remains the same DAY lighting. Do not alter lamp states or the colors of the remaining objects.
Maintain Image 1's matte gouache strokes, dry-brush marks, slightly wobbly colored-pencil edges and limited muted palette. Full-bleed landscape at the same native dimensions. No text, UI, plaques, frames, borders, people, glow, bloom or photorealism.
annotation_notes: Third actual processing round (initial real1 was only a visual annotation). Tree/vine ownership made disjoint; pale flower hues included through 255; crescent uses actual brown source contour instead of rectangular wall patch. Raster-run polygons encode actual native hard-mask rows; no art pixels generated.
